description: The league made it clear that Ball's rather unique footwor
body:
The league made it clear that Ball's rather unique footwork was not a legal move
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 22, 2026

    4:33 pm ET

            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Getty Images
            
            

    
        LaMelo Ball's debut with the Minnesota Timberwolves was a resounding success as the offense looked as advertised in a 131-106 destruction of the Miami Heat on the road. Ball scored 21 points and had six assists in a supporting role to Anthony Edwards' 45-point eruption, and also authored one of the early viral moments of the season with a hilarious uncalled travel on a double stepback 3. 
Richard Jefferson and Tim Legler laughed about it immediately on the TV broadcast and the clip swept across social media with fans wondering how that could possibly not be called a travel in real time -- including LaMelo's own brother, Lonzo Ball.

        
            
                Familiar faces, new places: Grading debuts for Giannis Antetokounmpo, Kawhi Leonard, other NBA stars
                
                    John Gonzalez                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
The official account of the NBA's referees, which is not known for jumping in on the fun, couldn't help but make light of the responses to Ball's, um, unique footwork going uncalled by confirming that it was not a legal move and should indeed have been whistled for an egregious travel.
Everyone can laugh about that missed call happening in a 25-point blowout, but with an official right there behind Ball watching the play, this one is hard to figure out how it went uncalled. 
The best explanation is that it was opening night for everybody, including the referees, who are locked in on new points of emphasis like illegal screens and push-offs, but need to remain vigilant for the rare double stepback attempts.

description: Martinez will face off against Brewers ace Jacob Misiorowski on Friday in Milwaukee

        In Game 1 of the 2026 World Series on Friday night, the Tampa Bay Rays will counter Milwaukee Brewers starter Jacob Misiorowski with a surprise choice: veteran right-hander Nick Martinez. Rays manager Kevin Cash announced the decision on Thursday. "When Nick pitches, we win," Cash said.The 36-year-old Martinez is coming off a strong regular season for the American League champs: 
For those efforts, which were good for a WAR of 3.9, Martinez earned his first career All-Star selection. "It's exciting," Martinez said on Thursday. "I think as a team, as a staff, we're confident in whoever we call up for the mound. It fell on me, and my job is just to rack up as many outs as we can and keep us in this ballgame."

        
            
                Jacob Misiorowski gets World Series Game 1 start for Brewers as he looks to reclaim his ace stuff
                
                    Mike Axisa                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
While Martinez is certainly a worthy choice to start Game 1, the decision was largely unexpected. Ace Drew Rasmussen had been available to start Game 1 on full rest, but going with Martinez affords Rasmussen an extra day of rest, which could be welcome given his career-high workload this season. Rasmussen instead is likely to go in Game 2. That means ALCS MVP and key deadline acquisition Freddy Peralta would start Game 3 back at Tropicana Field instead of pitching in Milwaukee, where he spent his entire career prior to this season. Specific rotation aside, if the series goes long enough, each of those three starters will get two full-rest turns against the Brewers. Martinez would be lined up to start a potential Game 5."We prioritized Drew getting an extra day," Cash said on Thursday. "He's had a pretty thick workload here and we've relied on him heavily. We know when he takes the ball, we're trying to get the full pitch allotment out of him. With Freddy, Freddy's workload in the CS was unique; we did ask him to come out of the bullpen between starts and felt like, how much of a toll does that take? I don't know. I thought he threw a really good ballgame in Game 6, but I did think that towards the end of that game, the velocities and stuff remained the same, but the command took a little bit of a dip."
Earlier in these playoffs, Martinez started ALDS Game 3 against the New York Yankees and ALCS Game 4 against the Cleveland Guardians. Across those two starts, he pitched to a 3.00 ERA with six strikeouts and three walks in nine combined innings.

description: Sunday's historic game at Stade de France will proceed as planned, with the NFL working alongside local authoriti
body:
Sunday's historic game at Stade de France will proceed as planned, with the NFL working alongside local authorities and increasing security
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 22, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:50 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        When the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints meet on Sunday in the NFL's first regular-season game hosted in Paris, they will do so with an intense civil unrest as the backdrop. Protests in the French capital will not impact the NFL Week 7 game, but they did lead to the cancellation of a fan event. The Steelers announced on Thursday that they will not hold the scheduled Steelers House gathering due to the protests.The event was scheduled to unfold over the weekend near the Bastille. There is an authorized march scheduled to begin at Place de la Bastille on Saturday.Sunday's game, meanwhile, will unfold at Stade de France in Saint-Denis, which is located just under six miles from the center of Paris and away from the scheduled demonstrations."Following recent events in the Bastille neighborhood, and after careful consideration, we felt it appropriate not to move forward with the planned Steelers House fan event in Paris," the Steelers said in a statement. "Preparations for Sunday's NFL Paris game at State de France continue as planned, with the NFL working closely with local authorities and partners on all operational and security matters."
There have thus far been no disruptions at NFL sites in the lead-up to Sunday's contest. While concerns over fan and player safety heightened over the last two weeks, the league insisted repeatedly that the game would go on as planned. The NFL first addressed the concerns on Oct. 14 when it stated it looks forward to welcoming fans to Paris later this month.One measure the NFL will enact, though, is an increase in security. NFL executive vice president of club business, international and league events, Peter O'Reilly, said this week that the security presence "will be heightened" as the league works in tandem with local authorities and the U.S. State Department. He said the NFL has had people in Paris since early October and that they are "being very vigilant in everything we do, in all of our planning on an hour-by-hour basis."Former NFL Security Committee member and current CBS Sports analyst Amy Trask said that while teams handle international travel differently from one another, they share similar rules with regard to curfews and activities outside of game day. Trask also detailed the role security plays in these overseas competitions.
"You've got security on site the moment people are approaching the venue," Trask said. "In other words, the security is not simply at the gate when people are entering the venue. There is security well outside of the venue. There is security before you even enter the parking lot, so there will be security throughout the area. Some of the security will be noticeable, recognizable. Some of the security will be undercover, meaning simply not in uniform, not dressed in a manner where you will immediately notice it is security. It was my experience that there is ample security at the NFL events. "... As I noted, when the games are in the United States, that's local security, municipal security, state security, national security. Now you will add to this Parisian security, French security as well."The protests have been ongoing for nearly a month and stem from discontent over the French school system and the nation's cost of living. Protesters, many of them students, called upon the government to address under-resourced schools, poor conditions and teacher shortages. They report, in some cases, that the schools are physically falling apart with crumbling ceilings, water in the walls and rats in the buildings.
Some protests have turned violent. Police arrested thousands of people in connection to the demonstrations and utilized tear gas, stun grenades and other crowd-control measures to address those protests that devolved from peaceful gatherings into riots, according to CBS News.

title: Eagles Saquon Barkley trade proposals: Giants, Bengals among six destinations - CBS Sports
description: A return to New York headlines six potential landing spots for Barkley if Philadelphia decides to reset its roste
body:
A return to New York headlines six potential landing spots for Barkley if Philadelphia decides to reset its roster
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 22, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:26 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Philadelphia Eagles might be at an inflection point in their championship contention window. Injuries to myriad starters, the loss of Jalen Hurts for the season, Lane Johnson's retirement and an offense that cannot seem to get off the ground raise questions about whether general manager Howie Roseman tears his roster down at the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline. If he does, star running back Saquon Barkley might be headed out of town.Trading Barkley would be the ultimate admission that the Eagles, as currently constructed, cannot achieve their goals. The financial impact of moving him will lock this franchise into a rebuild, as he carries a salary cap hit of $26.4 million in dead money for 2027. At the same time, the large sum of unusable cap space gives the Eagles leverage over trade partners in that they can drive up the price. Suitors could also be inclined to pay up, considering Barkley is only guaranteed $2.5 million next season and has no guaranteed money in the final year of his contract in 2028.On the other hand, Barkley is an aging running back who will turn 30 years old the week before the Super Bowl. He has not been able to replicate the magic of his career-best 2024 season, so the former NFL Offensive Player of the Year's best days may be behind him. That could make teams tepid about spending first-round draft capital in a potential trade.There are a number of teams that need help at running back, and despite the questions about Barkley's longevity, he would likely elevate their offenses to a significant degree.
Here are six potential trades that would move Barkley out of Philadelphia.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    New York GiantsGiants receive: Saquon BarkleyEagles receive: Cam Skattebo, 2027 second-round pick, 2027 sixth-round pickIn such a weak NFC East, the division-leading Giants have a path to the playoffs, but they need a functional run game to get there. Even with their abundance of options, it seems John Harbaugh does not know who to deploy at running back (especially if you ask Najee Harris). Reuniting with Barkley eliminates all questions. Plus, Harbaugh himself said this week that it would be "great" to be in a "Saquon Barkley circumstance" where the Giants had a clear-cut No. 1 ballcarrier.A return to New York makes plenty of sense for Barkley, but it would likely cost the Giants a premium to pull it off, given the intra-division nature of the trade. For multiple years of control of the Eagles' star running back, they may have to part with their own top running back asset in addition to meaningful draft capital.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Seattle SeahawksSeahawks receive: Saquon BarkleyEagles receive: Emanuel Wilson, 2027 third-round pick, 2027 fifth-round pickDeclining to bring Kenneth Walker III back in free agency has haunted the Seahawks, especially with Zach Charbonnet missing the first six games due to the torn ACL he sustained last season. The offense is far more ineffective than it was during last year's Super Bowl run because of the nonexistence of the run game, which ranks second-worst in EPA per rush. Charbonnet will return in Week 7, but he is not a bellcow back, and first-round rookie Jadarian Price is still on injured reserve. Seattle should make a run at a lead running back to revitalize an offense that, in its current form, is not good enough to make another deep postseason push.
Barkley's arrival would create a logjam at the position, so Seattle may try to send one back to Philadelphia. And with three third-rounders and three fifth-rounders in its coffers, those are the picks that make the most sense to move.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Minnesota VikingsVikings receive: Saquon Barkley, 2027 seventh-round pickEagles receive: 2027 third-round pick, 2027 fifth-round pick, 2027 sixth-round pickThe recent trade history between the Vikings and Eagles makes them sensible partners for another deal. Minnesota holds Philadelphia's upcoming third-round pick, while Philadelphia owns Minnesota's seventh-rounder in next year's draft thanks to the Jonathan Greenard trade they completed in April. Those picks could go back to their original homes if these teams do business with each other once again.
The Vikings' run game is serviceable and is in line for a boost with Jordan Mason set to come off injured reserve this week. But the pairing of Mason and Aaron Jones is only that: Serviceable. Barkley would be a clear upgrade for an offense that ranks in the bottom half of the league in scoring and yards per game. Bolstering that group should be a priority as Minnesota attempts to capitalize on its league-best defense and keep its perfect start to the season rolling.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Cincinnati BengalsBengals receive: Saquon BarkleyEagles receive: 2027 second-round pick, 2027 fifth-round pickThe name value alone of an offense that boasts Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Saquon Barkley would be tremendous. Imagine what it would deliver in terms of production. The Bengals' typically unstoppable unit is limited in 2026 by a run game that ranks just 27th in yards per game, so a boost on the ground would open all kinds of opportunities for Burrow downfield and rekindle that elite attack. Chase Brown has been a disappointment to the point where Samaje Perine is becoming an increasingly large part of the ground game. That signals a cry for help at the running back position.As the Bengals attempt to cash in during Burrow's prime, this is the time to mortgage the future and invest draft picks in splashy trades like one for Barkley.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Denver BroncosBroncos receive: Saquon BarkleyEagles receive: 2027 second-round pick, 2027 fifth-round pickSean Payton already reclaimed play-calling duties, but that might not be enough to save the Broncos' offense. Something else is clearly missing from this unit. Long-term assets like RJ Harvey and Jonah Coleman make the future of the running back group bright, but it is underperforming right now, and that is a problem for a team that has Super Bowl aspirations. An infusion of immediate help would lower J.K. Dobbins and Harvey a rung each on the depth chart, and perhaps that is precisely what the group needs while Coleman recovers on injured reserve.The Broncos are flush with 2027 late-round picks, so moving a Day 3 selection in addition to a second-rounder would not hurt.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Houston TexansTexans receive: Saquon BarkleyEagles receive: Woody Marks, 2027 seventh-round pick, 2028 second-round pickThe David Montgomery trade is aging like a bust of a move as he cedes work to Woody Marks in a disappointing run game. It would be an admission that the move did not pan out as expected if general manager Nick Caserio traded for another running back, but it might be a worthwhile one if it takes an otherwise surprisingly effective offense to another level. C.J. Stroud is playing the best football of his career and looks determined to pull the Texans out of the 0-4 hole they dug themselves into but might have trouble doing so if the ground game is a drag.
That the Texans hold the Eagles' 2027 seventh-round pick (which has already changed hands thrice) could aid in their pursuit of Barkley, even if it is just a throw-in as the final sweetener in the trade package.

title: NFL Hall of Famer Marshall Faulk announces Parkinson's diagnosis - CBS Sports
description: The Hall of Fame running back said he was diagnosed after noticing an issue with his hand and has been managing t
body:
The Hall of Fame running back said he was diagnosed after noticing an issue with his hand and has been managing the condition through treatment
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 22, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:10 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Marshall Faulk, an NFL legend and the coach at Southern University, revealed that he has been diagnosed with Parkinson's disease, a progressive disorder of the central nervous system affecting the body's movement. Faulk, 53, said that he has been dealing with the disease for about 18 months. He first realized that something was wrong when he was having issues with his hand while playing golf. He mentioned the issue to his doctor during a routine physical. "I was like, 'Wow, is that something?'" Faulk said on an episode of "Caring Neurologist" with Dr. Sandeep Thakkar. "'Is that normal?' And the doctor was— he literally was like, 'You need to go get checked.'"  Faulk is in good spirits and considers himself lucky because he got the diagnosis early. He said that it can be managed through treatment while comparing it to recovering from injuries during his NFL career. Since getting treatment, Faulk said that he has become more active, is sleeping more and that his life is relatively the same. He said that while he still experiences rigidity in his hands, the condition has not gotten worse. 
"The little tremors that I get, you know, they are what they are," he said. "I just pay attention to my gait, you know, while I walk, when I'm working out, my ability to balance. It's still where it is."  Faulk wants to advocate for people to seek help if they experience symptoms. Surprisingly, he said that he had not had a conversation about his diagnosis with his family or friends.  "If it comes a time to where my lifestyle changes, then I will," he said. "Then that conversation could be had. I'm functioning. I'm good. You know, I just I think I caught it early. I'm in a good place."  
Faulk was named Southern's coach on Dec. 1, 2025. He previously served as Deion Sanders' running backs coach at Colorado. A 2011 Pro Football Hall of Fame inductee, Faulk is widely considered one of the greatest running backs of all time. At San Diego State, he led the FBS in rushing three straight years. He finished second in the Heisman Trophy voting in 1992 and was fourth in the voting in 1993. Faulk was the No. 2 overall pick in the 1994 NFL Draft. He earned two Pro Bowls with the Colts before entering another stratosphere after he was traded to the Rams in 1999. That season, Faulk helped the Rams win the Super Bowl while becoming the second player to post 1,000 yards rushing and receiving in the same season. 
Faulk won league MVP in 2000 after he led the NFL in touchdown runs (18) and yards-per-carry average (5.4). He helped the Rams get back to the Super Bowl in 2001. A seven-time Pro Bowler and three-time All-Pro, Faulk retired after the 2005 season with 12,279 rushing yards, 6,875 receiving yards, 100 rushing touchdowns and 136 total touchdowns. He, Marcus Allen and Tiki Barber are the only players in NFL history with 10,000 rushing and 5,000 career receiving yards.

        One week after stunning No. 1 Georgia, Auburn will try to replicate that effort against No. 18 LSU. Auburn will have the Jordan-Hare Stadium crowd on it side, but the team faces an uphill battle in the pursuit of two major upsets.Going into its open date, Auburn was coming off a loss to Tennessee and needed something to build upon. An upset of the No. 1 team in the country on the road will certainly suffice, and now Alex Golesh must find a way to sustain that momentum. If Auburn is going to give itself a shot to slay SEC dragons in consecutive weeks, it will need to put the game on the shoulders of Byrum Brown again. He totaled 265 yards and a pair of touchdowns against the Bulldogs.On the other hand, LSU will have to be wary of entering a hostile environment given its recent history. The team has lost both of its road games this season, and Lane Kiffin's struggles away from home date back to when he first accepted the Ole Miss job. The Baton Rouge-based Tigers just shut out a shorthanded Mississippi State team in Death Valley, and Sam Leavitt played the first clean game of his LSU tenure. He'll need to replicate that performance in Auburn.Before this battle of the Tigers begins, we have everything you need to know about the matchup.
LSU vs. Auburn: Need to know  LSU's road woes: LSU is the clear favorite in this game, but it has struggled to win road games lately. The Tigers have dropped eight straight road games, which is the third-longest streak in school history. LSU is 0-2 on the road this fall, and Kiffin hasn't fared well away from home throughout his SEC coaching career. Between stops at Tennessee, Ole Miss and LSU, Kiffin is 14-16. Winning on the road is hard, but LSU can't make it even harder.Run, Bryum, run: If Auburn is going to put its best foot forward this weekend -- and for the rest of the season -- Brown will have to use his legs to create offense. That worked last week in Athens, as Brown toted the rock on 26 attempts, which included five sacks. The catch is that Brown will be exposed to more hits, which increases his risk for injury. Because of that, if Auburn can get its traditional run game rolling, that takes some of the workload off Brown's legs.Auburn trying to go back-to-back: Can Auburn pull off two stunners in a row? The Tigers haven't picked up wins over ranked teams in consecutive weeks since they rattled off three straight against Georgia, Alabama and Missouri in 2013. The trouble is that Auburn hasn't played well at home against ranked opponents of late, which is somewhat surprising given the general mystique around Jordan-Hare Stadium. The team is 1-9 in its last 10 home games against top-25 teams.

LSU's defense is athletic enough to contain Brown, and the offense is capable of putting up big numbers. No. 16 USC, which has rebounded from the Oregon loss with back-to-back wins, seeks to improve its road record to 3-0 on Saturday night in Wisconsin
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 22, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:01 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        When you look around the Big Ten these days, there's a lot of uncertainty. Nearly half the league is down to its backup quarterback, whether due to injury or by choice. The only undefeated team in the conference is UCLA, while Oregon's conference title hopes are hanging on by a thread. Ohio State just picked up a huge win, but faces the prospect of being without Julian Sayin for the rest of the season.It's chaos, and when chaos is around, there's a chance someone unexpected will emerge and take advantage of it. So while No. 16 USC's trip to Madison this weekend to face Wisconsin might not be the headliner game of the weekend, it's a chance for two teams to step forward and stake a claim in the conference.USC has won two straight since dropping a game to Oregon, and perhaps most surprisingly, one of those wins has come on the road. The Trojans are 2-0 outside the Coliseum, which has been a serious problem for them during Lincoln Riley's tenure. Now they're back on the road facing a Wisconsin team coming off its first Big Ten loss at UCLA last week.The winner stays in the Big Ten title race with a chance to capitalize on the chaos. The loser will have to hope for a lot more chaos to befall the rest of the league going forward.
USC vs. Wisconsin: Need to know  Wisconsin has struggled with USC: They haven't shared a conference for long, but there is familiarity with these programs. Familiarity Wisconsin would sooner forget. USC is 7-1 all time against the Badgers, with the lone loss coming in the 2015 Holiday Bowl. They've only played once as Big Ten foes, and USC won that game 38-21 in Los Angeles during the 2024 season. As for the trip to Camp Randall, USC has won both the games in Madison, though the last meeting came in 1965. NCAA eligibility rules change every day, but I'm pretty sure none of the players who played in that game have remaining eligibility.  Lincoln Riley is good off a bye: While Wisconsin was in Los Angeles losing to UCLA last week, USC was in Los Angeles chilling on the couch watching. That's typically been a good thing for the Trojans. Under Lincoln Riley, USC is 5-1 coming off a bye and has won three straight.  Wisconsin has performed poorly in these spots of late: Wisconsin has played six home games against AP-ranked opponents under Luke Fickell. It has won only once in those six games. That win came last season against No. 24 Washington. As for the five losses, four of them have come by at least 14 points, though all four of them were against top-4 teams in the poll.
Where to watch USC vs. Wisconsin live  Date: Saturday, Oct. 24 | Time: 7:30 p.m. ET  Location: Camp Randall Stadium -- Madison, Wisconsin  TV: NBC | Live stream: Fubo (try free)USC vs. Wisconsin prediction, picks  Wisconsin is probably looking at the weather forecast for this game and wondering what it did to offend the weather gods. If there was any time to wish for temperatures in the 40s with biting wind, it's when USC is coming to town. Instead, the forecast is calling for temperatures in the 60s with a manageable breeze. Still, even if the weather won't have an oversized impact, I like the under here. USC may have won its two road trips so far this season, but the offense didn't look great against Penn State, and this Wisconsin defense is good. I also don't have much faith in the Wisconsin offense.  Pick: Under 50.5

        Life in the new SEC is proving to show its teeth as Alabama finds itself in a must-win scenario after two straight defeats, needing a victory against Texas A&M to avoid falling out of the College Football Playoff picture before Halloween. After back-to-back losses to Georgia and Tennessee, Alabama is looking to avoid a three-game losing streak for the first time since 2007 (Nick Saban's first year as head coach), and Kalen DeBoer is hoping to avoid the first three-game losing streak of his entire head coaching career. The good news is that Alabama is welcoming an unranked Texas A&M team, and the Crimson Tide are carrying an 89-game winning streak against unranked teams. For Texas A&M, the path to falling from top-10 in the preseason to unranked highlights what has become one of the most disappointing seasons of the Aggies' SEC era. Ever since standing at 11-0 heading into the rivalry week in 2025, Texas A&M has lost each of its next four games against ranked opponents. The Aggies got to score some touchdowns and sing the fight song after blanking The Citadel 41-0, but when it comes to national attention, the failures in these spotlight opportunities have greatly changed the public's view of this team. The desperation for both these teams to avoid making their recent skids worse should spark some urgency, which always adds intensity to Saturdays in the SEC.
  Alabama vs. Texas A&M: Need to know  Alabama is dealing with multiple key injuries on offense: The Crimson Tide need that off week in the worst way, and at the beginning of the week multiple offensive starters are questionable for Saturday's game against Texas A&M after missing action in the loss at Tennessee. The most notable might be star wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams, who was injured in the loss to Georgia and is officially dealing with head and leg injuries. Coleman-Williams is the team leader in touchdown catches (4) and prior to his injury had more catches or yards than anyone else on the team, so maybe it's not a surprise that his absence against the Vols coincided with Keelon Russell's least-productive passing game of the season (147 yards). However, the issues could be starting up front, as Alabama was also struggling to deal with the loss of starting center Racin Delgatty, who was also injured in the Georgia loss. Delgatty's replacement against Tennessee was freshman Mal Waldrep, and facing the Vols' vicious defensive front in a raucous rivalry road atmosphere went about as well as you might predict for a freshman in his first career start.   Marcel Reed looking to recapture his best form after struggles in 2026: According to CBS Sports Research, Texas A&M quarterback Marcel Reed has the fewest passing yards per game (175.3) in FBS this season among quarterbacks with at least 200 pass attempts. That follows a 2025 season in which Reed won 11 games as the team's starter, averaging 243.8 passing yards per game and finishing with 31 total touchdowns. When former offensive coordinator Collin Klein left to take the head coaching position at his alma mater, Kansas State, the decision to promote from within aligned with the idea of leaning on continuity for a talented quarterback coming off a breakthrough season. Instead, what has followed is nine total touchdowns to six interceptions through seven games, a 55.7% completion percentage (last in the SEC), and the aforementioned lack of production that ranks among the worst in FBS. Trends point to a turnaround for Alabama in Tuscaloosa: While it has been a while since we have seen the Crimson Tide stack up defeats like they have this month, the overall trends show this matchup and this setting as favorable for Alabama. Kalen DeBoer is 16-2 as Alabama's coach in home games and just 9-8 away from Bryant-Denny Stadium, and Alabama is 13-3 against Texas A&M all-time and has only lost to the Aggies once in Tuscaloosa (Johnny Manziel's 29-24 upset in 2012). Neither team is in its best shape right now, but at least Alabama gets to play this SEC showdown in a comfortable setting where it's experienced much more success than the visitor.
Where to watch Alabama vs. Texas A&M live  Date: Saturday, Oct. 24 | Time: 3:30 p.m. ET  Location: Bryant-Denny Stadium -- Tuscaloosa, Alabama  TV: ABC | Live stream: Fubo (try free)  Alabama vs. Texas A&M prediction, picks  The Crimson Tide might be running on fumes here, playing their eighth game in eight weeks, especially considering the physical toll that comes with facing teams like Georgia and Tennessee. And while Texas A&M may be well off pace from preseason expectations and suffering from underwhelming performance, the Aggies are still a team with athletes and SEC-caliber bodies. A properly motivated Texas A&M team can make life a little bit harder for Alabama, even with the advantages they have on paper. For that reason, I could see this game being a little bit lower-scoring, with points tough to manufacture in what is ultimately an Alabama win. Pick: Under 50.5

Chesney is just the second head coach in FBS history to start his tenure 6-0 for a team that was coming off a 9-loss season. The other was Curt Cignetti with the Hoosiers in 2024. Both coaches came from James Madison and immediately ignited struggling Big Ten outfits. It's been a tougher road for Fitzgerald, the former longtime Northwestern coach who returned to the sideline this season after three years away from the college game. The Spartans' last two losses have come by a combined total of four points against Illinois and Northwestern. Michigan State is now seeking to avoid starting 0-5 in Big Ten play in back-to-back seasons for the first time in program history as it heads west for its first road game against UCLA since 1974. 
   UCLA vs. Michigan State: Need to know   Turning to Dieffenbach: UCLA starting quarterback Nico Iamaleava suffered a season-ending knee injury in the Bruins' Week 6 win over Oregon, leaving the Bruins in the hands of Ty Dieffenbach. The Cal Poly transfer held his own in UCLA's 17-7 win over Wisconsin last week and profiles similarly to Iamaleava. At 6-foot-6, he can see over the defense, and he takes long strides as a runner. His 264 passing yards against the Badgers marked a season-high for UCLA's passing game. Revitalizing the run: UCLA rushed for 200-plus yards in each game during its 4-0 start before getting slowed down in wins over Oregon and Wisconsin the past two weeks. The Bruins totaled just 140 yards on the ground against the Ducks and dipped to a season-low 120 against the Badgers. Wisconsin limited UCLA star Wayne Knight to 23 yards on 13 carries. If the Bruins are going to reach the full potential they flashed during the season's first half, getting the most out of Knight will be pivotal, especially now that UCLA is using its backup quarterback. Playoff implications: UCLA has a 28.4% chance of making the College Football Playoff entering the game, according to the CBS Sports CFP Forecaster. That mark improves to 35.2% with a win but plummets to 11.4% with a loss. Because of their light schedule strength, the Bruins would be in grave danger of missing the playoff at 10-2. A 5-1 (or 6-0) finish will likely be required for this team to reach the 12-team field.

The Spartans are capable of slowing down the Bruins' rushing attack, which is already trending in the wrong direction. It's hard to imagine the Spartans scoring enough to win the game outright against UCLA's stout defense. But a two-touchdown spread is a lot to cover for a Bruins team playing with its backup quarterback. Week 7 presents another round of difficult decisions for Fantasy managers, with four teams on bye, injuries reshaping depth charts and several big-name players facing matchups that could limit their production. As we approach the halfway point of the Fantasy regular season, every lineup decision becomes increasingly important.Braelon Allen is among the players worth trusting this week, with Breece Hall's injury opening the door for another strong performance against a vulnerable Dolphins run defense. Meanwhile, Woody Marks could benefit from an expanded workload in Houston, and Bryce Young continues to make a compelling case as a reliable Fantasy starter.On the other side, Patrick Mahomes faces a difficult matchup against Seattle, while Michael Wilson and Jameson Williams carry concerns despite their opportunities in their respective offenses. Even familiar names aren't automatic starts when defensive schemes, playing time and offensive tendencies work against them.That's where Dave Richard's Week 7 matchup breakdown comes in. From defensive coverages and pass-rush pressure to backfield workloads and target distribution, we'll examine the factors that matter most to help you identify trustworthy starters, avoid potential disappointments and make the best possible lineup decisions.

As Drake Maye's numbers have gotten hot, so too have Hunter Henry's. In the past three weeks Henry has turned 14 targets into a 12-154-2 stat line and more importantly 11-plus PPR points per game. He's become a go-to in the red zone for Maye, getting first reads and leading the team with four targets near the paint. He especially seemed to be on the same page as Maye on their touchdown last week. Henry has also become a short-area outlet when Maye's been pressured and/or needs to check the ball down -- six of his 14 targets have come in those specific situations since Week 4. While it means there aren't a lot of plays designed for Henry, it's still two good roles for an older, slower tight end, especially on a short week versus a depleted defense. Chicago has allowed an 86% catch rate to tight ends in the red zone this year with Kyle Pitts cashing in twice on them last week. Henry is a low-end starter.  Caleb Williams had two 2-yard runs, had a season low 3.23-second time to throw rate and a season low with Ben Johnson, 3.9-yard average depth of throw against the Falcons last week. That tells me he's still not 100% recovered from his hamstring injury, but it didn't quite turn him into a game manager. Five of his six biggest gains involved him holding the ball for at least three seconds, be it because he moved out of the pocket or not, and that doesn't include his 14-yard touchdown to Colston Loveland, where he escaped pressure and did the whole hold-and-throw-cross-body thing that he seems to live and die by. Williams is dangerous if he's mobile, but his Fantasy upside is lowered if he won't run downfield. The Patriots pass rush has been inconsistent all year but they tend to rack up sacks against statue QBs. Even with a couple of question marks along his O-line, Williams should be able to overcome their pressure and hit targets downfield. Last week, he completed all 26 of his throws for 255 yards when he wasn't pressured. That's bad news for the Patriots and good news for Williams. Luther Burden III had a great stat line last week -- 8-95-0 on eight targets -- but he didn't start, and he played just 39% of the snaps and ran a route on just 44% of Williams' dropbacks, both season lows. This happened because the Bears played with two or more tight ends on 67% of their plays, their second-highest mark of the season. Burden played just five snaps with Colston Loveland and Cole Kmet -- and had his biggest play of the day on one of them! Chicago has leaned into multiple tight end sets in three of their past five games, be it because of weather (Week 2), game script (Week 4), or to give its QB added pass protection (last week). Only the Raiders have felt the need to use a lot of multiple-tight-end formations against the Patriots this season. Because New England ranks 13th in pass-rush pressure rate and 16th in sack rate, the Bears may be more willing to attack downfield with receivers than stack big bodies. That's good news for Burden to keep his target volume flowing, especially since outside receiver Rome Odunze could have his hands full with Pats shutdown cornerback Christian Gonzalez. 
Bears offensive coordinator Press Taylor claimed this week that the Bears "weren't forcing it to (Colston Loveland) or anything like that." Taylor simply said, "The ball found him a couple times," meaning Loveland did what was needed to get open against the Falcons. He also had at least two designed targets, which helps. The Bears have seen man-to-man coverage on just 27 snaps all season, and Williams has yet to even target Loveland in man coverage this year, throwing at him at a 17.5% rate with poor efficiency versus man in 2025. The Patriots have played the second-most man-to-man coverage since Week 2 and third-most on the year, and they especially lean into it on third and short or third and medium downs. The only tight end to get more than 7.5 PPR points against the Pats this year was Brock Bowers. It's a concern when it comes to fully trusting Loveland this week, but you'd have to have some really good alternatives to pull him from lineups. MUST-START: D'Andre SwiftSTART: Drake Maye, Caleb Williams, Rhamondre Stevenson, A.J. This was foreseeable last week when he faced the blitz-heavy Bucs, but not in Week 5 against a muted Colts pass rush, nor should it be this way versus New Orleans. That's because the Saints haven't been a blitz-heavy team; they're bottom 10 in blitz pressure rate, bottom five in overall pass rush pressure rate and second-worst in non-blitz pressure rate. If anything, Rodgers should have a little more time to drop back. If he does, DK Metcalf would see the majority of long-distance targets; if/when he doesn't, then Germie Bernard's short-area target parade will continue. The Steelers are a better unit, but not by much. They employ fairly heavy zone coverage each week with a single-high safety lean, but they blitz less than 30% of the time and are bottom-10 in pass rush pressure rate with a modest 7.4% sack rate (boosted by corralling Jalon Daniels five times last week). Those factors might help Shough piece together a solid game, but it'll take an assist from the Steelers missing tackles or drawing penalties for him to post big stats. Shough and the Saints are also expected to be without guard Cesar Ruiz, a great pass blocker. The Raiders blitz less, pressure more, have one more sack than the Cardinals do and have one more Maxx Crosby than anyone else has. L.A. has seen its fair share of good pass rushers this year, but the only team that really affected them other than the Cardinals was the Broncos, and they put a ton of pressure on Stafford, whether they blitzed or not. The Raiders aren't quite as good as the Broncos are, and I don't expect the Rams to use their tight ends to block a ton, though that will be part of Colby Parkinson's role since he has 24 more pass pro snaps than Tyler Higbee has this season -- but also gets short targets after he chips a defender. Parkinson even has three red-zone targets when Adams is off the field compared to zero for Higbee. I wouldn't advocate for any single Rams tight end, but I can share that Higbee and Davis Allen are the two who run downfield routes at a much higher clip than Parkinson. The Raiders rank in the bottom three in completion rate (80.3%) and receiving touchdowns (six) allowed to tight ends, so chancing it on one of Parkinson or Higbee (in that order) as a bye-week TE makes some sense.
It's Kirk Cousins' tendency to throw to Michael Mayer when he's pressured that has kept Mayer's numbers up through the past three weeks -- 8 of his 20 total targets came on those kinds of plays, all short throws that Mayer turned into mostly gains of nine-plus yards. But that's his biggest role -- he had just six targets as a designed first read in his past three, and he hasn't seen a red-zone target since Week 3. Even without Poona Ford and Kobie Turner, the Rams should be able to get some pressure on Cousins with Aaron Donald, Byron Young and Josaiah Stewart. That would turn some throws into unscripted targets that Mayer can take advantage of, but that's also assuming this game stays close and the Raiders don't move into three-receiver formations late like they did against the Patriots. No one plays zone-heavy coverage more often than the Seahawks (90.7% of their snaps this season), and no one plays as much Cover-6 zone-heavy defense as the Seahawks (30.8% of their snaps). It would be uncharacteristic of coach Mike Macdonald to suddenly change things up and play more man-to-man coverage when his scheme has worked wonders for years, so get ready to watch Patrick Mahomes throw a bunch of short passes like he did last week. title: Jamal Wallace arrest: Utah DT suspended indefinitely amid rape accusation - CBS Sports
description: A probable cause affidavit reveals accusations of distributing intimate videos on Snapchat, though formal charges
body:
A probable cause affidavit reveals accusations of distributing intimate videos on Snapchat, though formal charges have not been filed following Wallace's release on bond
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 22, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:13 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Utah has suspended defensive tackle Jamal Wallace following an Oct. 11 arrest on suspicion of distributing intimate images via Snapchat. A probable cause affidavit obtained by The Salt Lake Tribune revealed that the woman also accused Wallace of rape.According to the document, the woman claims she met Wallace on Oct. 9 to discuss their relationship, which she described as "off-and-on" dating partners. She alleged that Wallace forced her to engage in various sexual acts, and she later realized that he had taken her phone to record videos.The woman alleges that Wallace sent video of the alleged rape to five people whom she'd been interacting with on Snapchat. After looking through the woman's phone, one officer discovered that Wallace recorded "two sexually explicit videos involving himself and the victim."As part of the investigation, the woman underwent a sexual assault examination.
Wallace has not been formally charged, and he was released on a $5,000 bond. A Utah spokesperson told The Salt Lake Tribune that it is aware of the allegations against Wallace, and he has been suspended indefinitely."We were made aware of the situation with Jamal Wallace on Oct. 11, and he was immediately placed on an indefinite suspension from the program," Utah said in its statement to the Tribune. "We take these matters seriously. As this is a pending legal matter, we have no further comment at this time."
In 2024, Wallace enrolled at Tennessee following a stint in junior college at Sierra College. Following the 2025 campaign, Wallace transferred to Utah and has played in just one game this season.

title: Colts' Chris Ballard firing: Mock trades for DT DeForest Buckner - CBS Sports
description: 'I'm sick and tired of the same song and dance every year,' Buckner told reporters postgame on Sunday.
body:
'I'm sick and tired of the same song and dance every year,' Buckner told reporters postgame on Sunday.
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 22, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:01 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Indianapolis Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon just let the rest of the NFL know a rebuild is coming in Indianapolis after the firing of general manager Chris Ballard on Monday.Irsay-Gordon ended Ballard's regime six games into his 10th season in charge. Indianapolis made the playoffs twice (2018 and 2020), going 1-2 in those two trips. The Colts' 72-82-1 regular-season record under his management ranked 17th in the league during Ballard's reign. Indianapolis's five straight missed playoffs represent the Colts' longest drought in over 40 years. An AFC South title never happened with Ballard.Now, the Colts are set to start over in 2027 with a new front office. Now is the time to rebuild since the 2027 NFL Draft is widely regarded as one of the most loaded classes in years. One issue is that the Colts don't have a first-round pick, thanks to trading their 2026 and 2027 first-round draft choices, along with wide receiver Adonai Mitchell, to the New York Jets last season in exchange for All-Pro cornerback Sauce Gardner.So, who could Indianapolis trade away to recoup some draft pick value? Well, three-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle DeForest Buckner basically put out a trade request after losing 26-20 at home against the previously 0-5 Tennessee Titans in Week 6. 
"I'm sick and tired of the same song and dance every year," Buckner told reporters postgame on Sunday.  
Buckner is 32 years old and a pending free agent next spring, but he could provide an immediate impact for a team looking to contend this season. His 4.0 sacks through six weeks are tied for the 10th most in the NFL, while his 19 quarterback pressures rank as the seventh most among defensive tackles in 2026.  For a real deal contender, Buckner could be worth a third-or fourth-round pick.   Who could inquire to be Buckner's new NFL landing spot? Let's take a look at four potential landing spots. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    San Francisco 49ersRecord: 6-0The 49ers make too much sense. That's where Buckner played his first four seasons, culminating in San Francisco losing Super Bowl LIV to the Kansas City Chiefs to conclude the 2019 season. He was traded to the Colts for a first-round pick in the 2020 offseason. San Francisco is going through its regularly scheduled injury catastrophe, so it could always use more bodies. The 49ers have the oldest roster in the entire NFL, with an average age of 28.5, and they once again lead the NFL in games missed because of injury, with 118 individual games. Adding another productive defensive line piece could pay dividends now and later. The last time the 49ers started 6-0 was Buckner's last season in San Francisco, which culminated in a Super Bowl trip. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Kansas City ChiefsRecord: 5-0The Kansas City Chiefs are in win-now mode every year with Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce leading their franchise. That's even more true in 2026 with free agent acquisition running back Kenneth Walker III, the reigning Super Bowl MVP, off to a historic start this season.One of their major weaknesses through five games is their pass rush. The Chiefs have the fourth-lowest sack rate in the entire NFL at 4.2%, and they're the only team in the whole league to not have a player with multiple sacks this season. Kansas City, as a team, has gone sackless in three of its first five games. Pairing Buckner with seven-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle Chris Jones could provide a major boost to both veterans as well as the Chiefs' sagging pass rush. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Minnesota VikingsRecord: 5-0  The Minnesota Vikings are 5-0 on the strength of defensive coordinator Brian Flores' aggressive unit. Flores' defense leads the NFL in:Scoring defense (12.8 points per game allowed)Third down defense (22.2% third down conversion rate allowed) Red zone defense (27.3% red zone touchdown rate allowed)Goal-to-go defense (33.3% goal-to-go touchdown rate allowed)Completion percentage allowed (53.2%)Touchdown-to-interception ratio allowed (3-6)Sack rate (9.8%)Pressure rate (46.4%)Blitz rate (69.8%)The Vikings' blitz rate of just under 70% is the highest by any team in any five-game span in the last 10 seasons, per CBS Sports Research. Some might call what Flores is doing early on this season "smoke and mirrors" with an outlier blitz rate, but adding a player like Buckner could solidify Minnesota's pass rush blitz or not. He could also be a nice mentor for rookie first-round pick defensive tackle Caleb Banks and another high-level contributor for Flores to incorporate into his scheme. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Green Bay PackersRecord: 4-2  The Green Bay Packers, a team that has been playing mix-and-match with an injury-plagued offensive line, have stabilized the unit with the same starting five combination for the last three weeks. That has also coincided with their defense leveling up during their current three-game winning streak, while not having to be on the field as often, thanks to the offense sustaining drives. Green Bay leads the NFL in scoring defense (11.3 points per game allowed) during the streak, but it needs more help along its defensive line as the season develops. 
Green Bay lost defensive tackle Javon Hargrave for the season with a torn Achilles, so it would make sense for them to place a call for Buckner. Adding Buckner to a defensive line that will get All-Pro edge rusher Micah Parsons back later in the year could give the Packers' defense the boost it needs to help power a deep playoff run in January and February.

title: 2026 World Series: Junior Caminero, Jackson Chourio emerging as national superstars - CBS Sports
description: In the words of their teammates, two of the best -- and youngest -- players on the Rays and Brewers are ready for
body:
In the words of their teammates, two of the best -- and youngest -- players on the Rays and Brewers are ready for the bright lights
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 22, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:49 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        MILWAUKEE -- World Series discussions often center around the superstars -- especially if there are those easy ones we can call "future Hall of Famers." Two years ago, when the Los Angeles Dodgers and New York Yankees faced off, there were at least five active players that fit the bill and probably a few more with a decent chance. This time around, the Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays don't have any surefire Hall of Famers. Christian Yelich is the closest thing, and he might be short (it's a different discussion for a different time).  I think there's a good argument to be made, however, that the best position player on each team is, in fact, a future Hall of Famer. It's far too early to make such a declaration, but they have the early foundation and the required talent. Both are emerging superstars, though one is a little more nationally established than the other (thank you, Home Run Derby). They'll get their spotlight together in this series. We're speaking, of course, about Junior Caminero of the Rays and Jackson Chourio of the Brewers. Now, they aren't unknowns. I'm not suggesting that. But I'll also excuse you if you don't regularly watch either of these teams. Regardless, we are all about to be blessed with a significant part of the next wave of incredible baseball talent. 
Caminero is a 23-year-old Dominican third baseman. His first full-time season was 2025, during which he clubbed 45 homers with 110 RBI. As an encore this season, he hit 42 home runs with 101 RBI. Don't mistake the line as regression. Though the power numbers dipped ever so slightly there, he raised his average by 12 points, his on-base percentage by 49 points and his walk rate by five percentage points, all while his strikeout rate dropped. To see this type of growth from one year to the next at age 23 while nearly maintaining his power leads me to believe there's an untapped extra gear in him as a player. We might well see him hit close to .300 next season and duplicate those 40 bombs. He also improved on defense, helping him vault to 5.7 WAR from last season's 4.3."I think the upside is just the consistency," Rays outfielder Cedric Mullins said on Thursday. "He's put some fantastic seasons together in back-to-back years. Even when he started off a little slow, he bounced back with a crazy hot streak. It's going to be exciting to see what he can do moving forward."
"Junior is a special player, special teammate," Rays manager Kevin Cash said earlier in the playoffs. "He's been incredible and would expect that, just as he's done every single stop throughout his career, whether it's playing winter ball or coming up, he's going to be very excited, motivated, and we'll rise to the occasion."
Caminero might well finish in the top two of MVP voting, behind favorite Yordan Alvarez, and I've seen enough to say with decent certainty that he's a future MVP. Rays catcher Liam Hicks, acquired at the trade deadline, raved about something as simple as getting to watch Caminero in batting practice every day, but focused specifically on his ability to adjust and adapt at the big-league level."That's the crazy thing, too: how much power he has, how many home runs he hits," Hicks said. "He doesn't strike out a lot; he makes a ton of contact. I think that part of his game is just crazy. He's got as much upside as anyone in the game."
Chourio, meanwhile, is a 22-year-old Venezuelan (and World Baseball Classic champion!) who signed an eight-year extension before he even debuted in the majors. He started playing professionally at age 17 in the Brewers system and was a top five prospect in all of baseball by 2023, when he was just 19. There's a five-tool superstar in here just waiting to have a monster breakout season. Here in 2026, he had his best year, but there's clearly more in the tank. Remember, he's only 22. Injuries held him to 127 games this year, but he still hit .291/.351/.487 (129 OPS+) with 27 doubles, 25 home runs, 75 RBI, 96 runs, 23 steals and 4.9 WAR. He's a Gold Glove finalist and he's gone 20-20 in all three of his MLB seasons so far. He can do it all. "Chourio is, he's special, man," Brewers pitcher Chad Patrick said on Thursday during media day. "When you watch him in the box, his presence, his tone, he's capable of being anything he wants to be in the box."His day-in, day-out is just happy. He's a happy guy."
"The ceiling he has is so high that we don't know if he'll ever hit it," reliever DL Hall said. "You know, just because he just keeps getting better and better and it seems like there's no limit."
"Playing with him every day for me and the rest of the bullpen, every time he gets up, we're like, 'he's probably gonna hit a homer.' Every single time he comes up to the plate, you just expect something special. It speaks to the work he puts in and how focused he is, especially at such a young age." It's impossible to miss the talent just oozing out of Chourio. There's an earned swagger that says we ain't seen nothin' yet. Another future MVP? He absolutely has the talent, even if he's further away than Caminero at this point -- and that's no insult. Chourio has also shown a flair for the dramatic."No moment's too big for Jack Jack," Brewers manager Pat Murphy said after NLCS Game 3, when Chourio hit a first-pitch home run off former Cy Young winner Blake Snell. "He's special."
Brewers pitcher Dustin May has seen his fair share of talented teammates, including the likes of Shohei Ohtani, Freddie Freeman, Mookie Betts, Cody Bellinger and Christian Yelich. And that's only naming his teammates who have won MVPs. "I can't say no," May said when CBS Sports asked if Chourio would join that list. "He's definitely got it in there, for sure. If he can put it together one year like I know he can, he'll win one.""I think [MVP upside] is there for sure," said Patrick. "He's learned the game over the last three years and he definitely has the upside to win it." 
Caminero and Chourio, the young studs of their respective clubs, are different players. The former is a corner infielder and prototypical middle-order slugger, even if he's more well-rounded than some might believe that term implies. The latter is an outfielder with great speed, capable of a 30-30 season as soon as next year, but he's unlikely to get up into the mid-40s in home runs the way Caminero figures to do annually. Caminero won't steal a ton of bases, while Chourio could well go for 40+ someday. But no matter the skill set, they have something undeniably in common: they're the best position players on their team at a tender, young age. The 2026 World Series is a showcase for these two uber-talented players. It probably won't be the last.
